brief.headline: Memory Super-Cycle Extends: HBM3E Prices +20%, DRAM/NAND Contracts Surge 58-75% QoQ in Q2 Amid Hyperscaler $700B Capex Wave
brief.summary: <cite index="8-3">Samsung Electronics and SK hynix raised HBM3E supply prices by nearly 20% for 2026</cite>, while <cite index="11-7,17-16">conventional DRAM contract prices will rise 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 and NAND Flash contract prices will jump 70-75% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="3-10">HBM3E will account for approximately two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026, while HBM4 gradually increases its share</cite>, with <cite index="3-18">SK hynix expected to achieve approximately 70% market share in HBM4 for NVIDIA's Rubin platform in 2026</cite>. <cite index="32-5,35-6">Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Alphabet collectively plan to spend roughly $700-725 billion on capital expenditures in 2026</cite>, driving structural memory demand. <cite index="21-13">SK hynix's market cap has climbed to about 85% of Samsung Electronics' market cap</cite>, reflecting SK's HBM dominance.
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix vs. Samsung remains correct but stretched. <cite index="4-8">SK hynix held 53% HBM market share in Q3 2025, compared to Samsung's 35%</cite>, and <cite index="3-12,3-13">SK hynix maintains 62% HBM shipment share as of Q2 2025 and will be the first HBM3E supplier for Google's TPU v7p and v7e</cite>. However, <cite index="4-8,6-20,6-21">Samsung received favorable feedback in Nvidia's HBM4 system-in-package tests, while SK hynix has already established HBM4 mass production framework</cite>. Positioning: rotate partial SK outperformance into Samsung HBM4 recovery theta; gap narrowing into 2H26 as Samsung ramps 12-layer HBM4. <cite index="21-2,21-4">Hana Securities warned SK hynix's market cap surpassing Samsung could signal a market bubble</cite>, with SK at 85% of Samsung's valuation already extreme.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="18-9,18-11">$755B in 2026 hyperscaler capex with memory consuming ~30% creates structural demand floor that did not exist in prior cycles; AI infrastructure demand has sold out 2026</cite>. <cite index="11-9,11-10">DRAM suppliers reallocating capacity towards AI-related applications; meaningful capacity expansion not expected until late 2027 at earliest</cite>. <cite index="13-7">Analysts project memory price rally poised to extend past 2028</cite>. Risk: Q2 price momentum (+58-75% QoQ) unsustainable at current velocity; PC/smartphone demand destruction visible.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="6-6,6-1">HBM3E will account for 66% of total HBM output in 2026, down from 87% this year; competitive inflection point expected with Rubin launch in 2H 2026</cite>. <cite index="6-10,6-11">Nvidia recently asked major memory suppliers whether they could deliver 16-layer HBM in Q4 2026, triggering internal planning around development schedules</cite>. <cite index="2-3,2-4">SK hynix set to complete first clean room at M15X fab in May 2026 and begin pilot operations; facility will manufacture both HBM3E and HBM4</cite>. <cite index="8-9">Google's TPU integrates eight HBM3E stacks per chip, while Amazon's Trainium3 uses four stacks</cite>. CoWoS remains bottleneck: <cite index="42-2,42-6">TSMC's entire CoWoS lineup at full capacity, with both CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix push HBM3E prices +20% for 2026 amid hyperscaler ASIC ramp
news_pulse.implication: HBM ASP trajectory exceeds consensus; Google TPU v7, Amazon Trainium3 driving 8-stack/4-stack incremental content beyond Nvidia H200. Pricing power persists into 2026 despite HBM4 ramp.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contracts +58-63% QoQ Q2, NAND +70-75% QoQ as memory shortage intensifies
news_pulse.implication: Sequential price momentum decelerating from Q1's record +90-95% DRAM spike but absolute levels crushing client demand. NAND now outpacing DRAM QoQ for first time; enterprise SSD allocation exhaustion.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex revised to $700-725B for 2026, nearly double 2025 spend
news_pulse.implication: Microsoft $190B, Meta $125-145B, Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B. Component price inflation ($25B at MSFT alone) embedding 2026-2027 memory ASP floor. No demand signal weakness.

news_pulse.headline: SK hynix market cap reaches 85% of Samsung; Hana warns bubble risk if overtakes
news_pulse.implication: SK represents 22% of KOSPI (all-time high vs. 13% SK Telecom 2000 peak). Valuation stretched but earnings-backed: Samsung/SK combined = 48% KOSPI market cap, 72% profit share. Contrarian signal if SK > Samsung.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia asks suppliers about 16-layer HBM delivery in Q4 2026, pulls forward transition
news_pulse.implication: 16-layer HBM4/4E discussions exploratory but signal Rubin urgency. Technical hurdle step-function higher than 8→12 layer. Hybrid bonding vs. MR-MUF battle shaping Samsung catch-up vector.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity fully booked; Nvidia locks >60% through 2027
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging remains choke point for HBM4 ramp. CoWoS-L expansion centered at AP7/AP8; AMD/Google/Amazon competing for remaining 40%. HBM suppliers must sync production to TSMC allocation.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung union plans 18-day strike starting May 21; HBM supply risk flagged
news_pulse.implication: Samsung labor action risk emerging after court partial injunction. Disruption to HBM qualification/ramp timeline would widen SK Hynix gap further; watch Nvidia commentary on dual-sourcing urgency.

news_pulse.headline: SK hynix M15X fab clean room completes May 2026; HBM3E/HBM4 dual production
news_pulse.implication: M15X pilot ops begin on schedule; 1c DRAM lines for HBM4E planned. SK positioning for sustained 50%+ HBM share through dual-generation execution. Capacity edge vs. Samsung/Micron widens.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="23-2,23-8,23-10">Eight asset managers plan to list 16 single-stock leveraged and inverse ETFs tied to Samsung and SK Hynix on May 27, marking first time single-stock leveraged ETFs listed in South Korea</cite>. <cite index="29-20">SK Hynix leveraged ETF has AUM of approximately $5.4B, world's largest single-stock leveraged product; Samsung leveraged ETF ~$1.65B</cite>. Retail froth indicator: <cite index="22-2,22-3">391 out of 1,107 domestic ETFs hold Samsung, 386 hold SK Hynix; about one-third of all locally listed ETFs contain at least one of the two</cite>. <cite index="25-7,25-8">KOSPI triggered sell-side sidecar May 18-19, second consecutive session after March US-Iran war spike</cite>. Volatility regime shifting; gamma squeeze risk on May 27 ETF launch.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung union strike progression (May 21 start date); any HBM production impact commentary from supply chain
KOSPI sidecar triggers and margin call cascades if Samsung/SK correct >5% ahead of leveraged ETF launch May 27
Nvidia/hyperscaler commentary on CoWoS allocation and willingness to pay for 16-layer HBM pull-in
TrendForce/DRAMeXchange spot pricing updates for DDR5/LPDDR5X (watch for demand destruction signals)
China YMTC or domestic DRAM capacity announcements (policy response to Korean duopoly pricing power)
